title: Planckian dissipation: definitions and inference
summary: A linear resistivity does not by itself measure a Planckian lifetime. Specify the relaxation channel, residual rate, frequency convention and transport model.

claims.statement: “Planckian” commonly describes a specified relaxation rate on the scale $k_BT/\hbar$, with a dimensionless coefficient of order unity. It is not a theorem inferred from a resistivity curve that happens to be linear in temperature. Transport, optical, single-particle, thermalization and quantum-chaos times probe different correlation functions and need not be equal.
claims.conditions: A lifetime must specify transport/optical/single-particle/thermal/chaos channel, residual term and h-versus-hbar convention. Single-band Drude extraction assumes appropriate n and m*.
claims.verificationScope: Conceptual distinction checked against Hartnoll-Mackenzie arXiv v3 sections 4-5; experimental universality is not established.

claims.statement: Maldacena, Shenker and Stanford bound the growth of a regularized out-of-time-order correlator by $\lambda_L\leq 2\pi k_BT/\hbar$. Their argument assumes analyticity and boundedness in a thermal complex-time strip, controlled factorization errors, and a separation between dissipation and scrambling times. It constrains a quantum-chaos exponent, not a measured charge-transport relaxation rate. Identifying $\lambda_L$ with $1/\tau_{\mathrm{tr}}$ requires additional model-specific justification; the bound does not establish a universal transport coefficient $\alpha=1$.
claims.conditions: Thermal quantum systems with a suitable regularized correlator, analyticity/boundedness, controlled factorization error and separated dissipation/scrambling scales. The bound applies in the exponential-growth regime above the error; no transport-time identification is assumed.
claims.verificationScope: Selected primary passages: Maldacena-Shenker-Stanford Eq. (2.5), sections 4.1-4.2 and 4.3.3. Transport distinction cross-checked against Hartnoll-Mackenzie arXiv v3 section 5; no independent proof verification.
